C9000228.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 228 (Continuum phase transitions for radial pair potentials.; papers: A continuum temperature singularity for a radial pair potential; A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/228.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_ALG_MAIN.statement: Algebraic-decay thm:main: one bounded continuous stable radial potential has tail O(r^(-3-1/32)) and a common canonical inverse-temperature corner on an open density interval centered at 5p/3.

C_CORE.statement: The bounded core has shell clique number at most four and yields the common quadratic small-cell and total-density stability estimates, including permitted deletions.

C_THERMO.statement: Every bounded-core family member, including countable sums, has all-sequence canonical and physical grand-pressure limits and partial density duality.

C_TAIL.statement: Canonical quadratic stability gives a uniform grand-count tail with auxiliary quadratic coefficient between zero and 2(A+1), without local moment input.

C_MOMENTS.statement: The conditional-cell exponential-moment bootstrap gives volume-independent mixed occupation moments for all permitted signed-reference deletions and interpolations; absolute interpolation and mass-continuity follow.

C_TRANSFORM.statement: Ideal attraction is the density quadratic transform; maximizing shifts are attained, nonnegative, uniformly bounded, and its increment is O(a).

C_SLOPES.statement: At positive mass the active-point parabolic inequality fixes all reference density supports to the active shift, and the transformed subdifferential is exactly the convex hull of active-branch supports.

C_DELETE.statement: Aligned finite-range reference deletion and finite-box reference pressure errors are bounded by B R0/s, using absolute interaction differences.

C_KERNEL.statement: For a nonnegative compactly supported C1 kernel the upper row sum is at most 1+Cw s/R, and the off-diagonal lower row sum of interior boxes is at least 1-Cw s/R.

C_RANGE_UPPER.statement: The block-product grand sum gives Q_full <= T_a Q_ref + B R0/s + B a s/R + log(floor(D s^3)+2)/(t s^3), uniformly over all reference families.

C_RANGE_LOWER.statement: Independent whole-box reference ensembles and Jensen give Q_full >= T_a Q_ref - B R0/s - B a s/R, without convergence of the finite-box density or any pressure differentiability.

C_RANGE.statement: Theorem k:range holds with constants independent of R0, all preceding masses and ranges and their finite or countable number, and every positive added mass a with total mass <= A+1.

C_RANGE_SHARP.statement: The same family satisfies the sharper error bound C min(a,sqrt(a R0/R)); this is a proposed independently proved strengthening, not a novelty-certified campaign result.

C_RANGE_CORE.statement: Finite symmetric-kernel quadratic domination, the product-density lower algebra, and two-sided error balancing hold over the reals for every finite index set and all nonnegative masses.

C_INIT.statement: The bounded-core pressure converges as t grows to max(0,p h,4p h-9p), and its first ideal transform has separated generating supports near three noncollinear slopes.

C_PERSIST.statement: Algebraic-decay m:one-step preserves separated generating support groups with slope-radius loss 2 delta/(l a)+a U_*^2/2 and parameter-radius loss S_* a.

C_ALG_CONSTRUCT.statement: The explicit doubly exponential range schedule and summable masses preserve a common support ball and produce a single stable potential with the stated power tail.

C_CORNER.statement: Two pressure supports with the same positive density and different inverse-temperature coordinates imply distinct finite one-sided canonical slopes; a common support ball supplies a density interval.

D_CORE.statement: The divergent-core companion shell graph and core yield common superstability after allowed cell deletions.

D_THERMO.statement: Companion prop:thermodynamics supplies canonical and grand limits and partial duality for its divergent-core family.

D_TRANSFORM.statement: Companion prop:transform supplies the attained density transform and supporting-gradient description.

D_MOMENTS.statement: Companion prop:moments and prop:tail give uniform occupation control and continuity under the mass of the remaining attractive tail.

D_KAC.statement: Companion prop:kac needs only locally uniform Kac convergence for each fixed finite-range reference and fixed added mass, not the quantitative estimate C_RANGE.

D_INIT.statement: Companion prop:free-pressure and prop:initial-triple give the three-branch initial generating supports and common slope ball.

D_PERSIST.statement: Companion lem:persistence preserves the common slope under a pressure error of order a^2 followed by an ideal mass of order a.

D_CONSTRUCT.statement: Choosing masses before sufficiently large ranges via qualitative Kac convergence gives one divergent-core potential with an integrable o(r^-3) tail and a limiting common pressure-support ball.

D_MAIN.statement: Companion thm:main: one admissible radial divergent-core potential has a common beta_c in (1/2,3/2) with strict canonical temperature corners on an open positive-density interval.
